A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DOTS research and contain complete, readable main texts and Appendices A–D. Equations, figures, tables and relocated passages can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic simulations, CausalTime evaluations and ablations in Section 5 and Appendices B–C.

after.justification: v2 retains the original simulations, CausalTime results and ablations, including the supplementary empirical analyses.

M1.justification: Sections 4.2–4.4 and Algorithm 1 retain the same lag embedding, diffusion-based Hessian ordering, aggregation, temporal constraints and CAM pruning. Algorithm 1 moves relative to its explanation without changing its steps.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same nonlinear synthetic time series and CausalTime Medical, AQI and Traffic datasets. The lag range and dataset names added to the abstract already appeared in v1's experimental description.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Figures 6–8, Table 2 and the appendix comparisons. Both exclude TiMINo from window-graph results and SCORE, DAS and NoGAM from Table 2 because of memory limits.

E3.justification: Both retain the same simulation grid, CausalTime preprocessing, graph representations and evaluation metrics. Appendix D retains the same maximum-lag settings and ordering counts, including 20 orderings for CausalTime.

E4.justification: The ordering-count ablation, temporal-constraint comparison, maximum-lag and voting-threshold sensitivity studies, and ordering-diversity analyses are retained unchanged in Section 5.6.3 and Appendices B–C.

E5.justification: Both report 10 repetitions for the main simulations, 500 for the ordering-count experiment and 100 for the appendix ablations. Confidence-interval reporting is unchanged.

E6.justification: The numerical tables and plotted results match across versions, including the appendices. Table 2 retains DOTS scores of 0.548, 0.457 and 0.349 on Medical, AQI and Traffic, respectively, with an average of 0.451.

T1.justification: Assumptions 1–5, Proposition 1 and its proof and example, the diffusion-frequency derivation, and Appendix A's order-theory definitions are unchanged.

C1.justification: The multiple-ordering contribution, transitive-closure argument and comparative performance claims retain their meaning and scope. The abstract's added benchmark details specify evaluations already documented in v1.

C2.justification: The result interpretations and limitations remain the same, including untested assumption violations and dependence on CAM pruning. Replacing 'unconfoundedness' with 'sufficiency' in Section 5.7 does not change the stated applicability boundary.

D1.justification: Appendix D retains the same hyperparameters and implementation sources. The DOTS repository link added to the abstract was already supplied in Section 5.1 of v1; no new resource or access information is introduced.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive research positioning in Section 6 are unchanged. The added publication header and OpenReview link are publication metadata.

P1.justification: v2 makes limited grammar, spelling and terminology edits, adds existing benchmark details to the abstract, and updates publication and acknowledgment text. Appendix B.2 changes 'score-matching methods' to 'ordering-based methods'; the section structure remains intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds publication headers and reflows text and displays. For example, Table 2 moves from page 16 to 17 and Figure 9 from page 17 to 18. The figures and tables retain their content and visual design.

improvement.justification: v2 provides small editorial conveniences through clearer abstract details, terminology corrections and a more prominent existing code link. The method, theory, empirical evidence and reproducibility information, including the appendices, remain unchanged. The copyedits and layout adjustments do not establish a meaningful net change in overall paper quality.
